subject: Re: Live demo — intermittent streaming silence and timeouts (urgent)
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@redprism.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-29T15:12:00Z
Subject: Live demo — token stream stopped twice during customer Q&A

Camila, 

We had you on for the live demo today with the RedPrism engineering team (11:10 PT). During the Q&A the token stream stalled twice for ~7-12s and then resumed — customers saw blank lines and a spinning loader. We also saw a few 502s in the browser console immediately after the stalls.

Key observations from our side:
- Latency spiked from ~120ms to ~3s for chunks when the stall happened.
- Error rate ~7% for the live session (small sample).
- Overall throughput dropped ~60% during the incident window.

This is a high-visibility POC; the CTO and procurement are on the thread. We need a quick explanation and mitigation — they want to avoid more disruptions. Attached a screenshot from the console and a short clip of the client behavior.

Can your team confirm whether this is a client-side issue or something on the Redwood streaming path (proxy / websocket / chunked transfer)? 

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform, RedPrism AI
[screenshot_1.png attached]

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@redprism.ai>, Alyssa Wong <alyssa.wong@redprism.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-29T15:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Live demo — token stream stopped twice during customer Q&A

Sanjay / Alyssa — thank you for the quick signal and the screenshot. Im very sorry this happened during the demo. I have looped in our on-call ops/engineering and vanessa for exec awareness.

Immediate ask: can you share the browser console logs and the exact demo session id (if available)? That will let us correlate proxy logs -> backend.

What were doing now:
- Stand up an ad-hoc war room (link to follow).
- Engineering will pull live proxy and worker logs for the session id and a 10m window around the stalls.
- If we see keepalive drops / proxy queues, we will push a temporary config bump (ws timeout / connection backlog) and enable the fallback to chunked SSE for that customer.

I will get back within 30 minutes with an initial triage. Again — very sorry and were on it.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-29T15:40:00Z
Subject: Escalation: RedPrism demo — streaming stalls, elevated error rate (needs exec attention)

Team — escalating to you because RedPrism (POC) hit two streaming stalls during a live demo with their engineering + CTO. This is time-sensitive: customer is evaluating for real-time inference in prod.

Summary:
- Event: repeated token-stream silence during a 40-minute demo (two visible stalls).
- Observed impact: client-perceived blank output + browser 502s, estimated error rate ~7% during window, latency spikes to ~3s for chunk delivery, throughput drop ~60%.
- Business risk: POC conversion / procurement decision likely influenced by reliability of streaming. Customer called this "unacceptable" for their real-time use case.

Requested action:
1) Exec visibility and permission to escalate priority with infra: we may need an emergency patch/rollback or high-priority config change on the streaming proxy.
2) Headcount/eng focus: ask that engineering allocate a small war room (ops engineer + runtime lead + support) to triage and apply a short-lived mitigation (scale + timeout bump + fallback).
3) Communication: I will run a customer-facing note and coordinate a follow-up demo window; any suggested wording appreciated.

Attachments: customer screenshot (sent), were pulling logs now and will attach log snippets.

Thanks,
Camila

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: support_oncall@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-29T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Escalation: RedPrism demo — streaming stalls, elevated error rate (needs exec attention)

Quick triage (initial):
- Reproduced short stall pattern in proxy logs: sustained backlog on websocket accept queue followed by abrupt connection tear (502) when the worker stalled on a KV-cache eviction path.
- Correlated worker logs show a hot-spot GC + quantization path lock during a model shard reload triggered by a background model-version sync (unrelated scheduled job).

Probable root cause: race between live request handling and model-sync job causing transient worker CPU/GIL pressure -> chunk emission pauses -> proxy connection timeouts. At scale this surface manifests as increased error rate and throughput collapse.

Immediate mitigations (I can push these now if approved):
- Temporarily disable model-version sync on the tenant and roll the job out off-peak. (config patch: commit a1f3c9b)
- Increase websocket read timeout and proxy accept backlog for the tenant's routing policy (config bump for demo tenant only).
- Scale worker pool + increase streaming concurrency by 2x for the tenant for the next 2 hours.
- Enable SSE (chunked) fallback in the SDK for the session if WS fails.

Attachments: log_snippet.txt (proxy + worker window), pcap_summary.pdf (short capture showing TCP stalls).

Suggested message to customer: short apology, explain were applying a temporary mitigation and schedule a follow-up demo in 24-48h. I will standby to run the war room at the link below.

War room: https://meet.redwood.com/warroom/rdp-downdraft-20260930

Grace O'Connor
Engineering Manager, Runtime Reliability
[log_snippet.txt attached] [pcap_summary.pdf attached]

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@redprism.ai>, Alyssa Wong <alyssa.wong@redprism.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, support_oncall@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T02:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Live demo — token stream stopped twice during customer Q&A

Sanjay / Alyssa — quick update and next steps. First, Im sorry again for the interruption earlier. We have: 

- Identified a likely race between an off-cycle model-version sync job and live request handling that caused transient worker stalls.
- Applied temporary mitigations: disabled the sync job for RedPrism, increased websocket timeouts and proxy backlog for the tenant, and scaled the worker pool x2 for the next 2 hours.
- Enabled chunked SSE fallback in the SDK for the affected session (so the UI shows progressive chunks if WS is unreliable).

Weve scheduled a short war room at 02:30 UTC (link below) to monitor live traffic and confirm the mitigations hold. Grace has attached logs and a short pcap summary to the thread.

Would you be available for a 30-minute follow-up demo tomorrow at 17:00 PT? If that works we will run it under the mitigations and capture end-to-end telemetry.

War room: https://meet.redwood.com/warroom/rdp-downdraft-20260930

Thanks for your patience — were prioritizing this until its resolved.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
